statement: A completed split reaches a durable terminal state and clears the tables transition row: SPLIT_SOURCE_DISSOLVING and completed phases modeled on merge dissolution, non-participating sibling partitions carried forward into the new epoch in the SAME change as the terminal state (a second split of an already-split table neither wedges the table nor strands sibling key ranges), partition_count set to oldCount + 1 at cutover, pending_partition_version withdrawn on FAILED, and SPLIT_COMPLETED emitted at terminal (not at plan time). doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/split-terminal-lifecycle.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — terminal-clear, sibling-carry-forward, partition-count, failed-withdrawal, and terminal-completion-event receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The terminal lifecycle state and sibling carry-forward MUST land as one change: shipping the terminal state without carry-forward converts the stuck-table wedge (F9) into silent sibling stranding (F1), and shipping carry-forward without the terminal state is unreachable. Model both on the merge path (dissolution phases, promoteSiblingPartitionVersion, terminal transition clearing).

A split that cannot prove its terminal transition clear landed must not advance in-memory state: persistTerminalTransitionClear and the FAILED pending-version withdrawal verify affectedRows (Tier 1 contract) and throw otherwise.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding terminal/carry-forward/withdrawal mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert checks) at quest terminal; no hand-authored metric values.
